name: Aider
summary: A terminal pair programmer that edits your repo through git commits, with any model you point it at.
description:
Aider works in a terminal, keeps a repository map of your code so it can reference files it has not been handed, and writes each accepted change as a real git commit with a message it generated. That commit-per-change behaviour is the design: you can revert a bad model edit with the same tool you use to revert a bad human edit, and history stays legible.

It is model-agnostic, so quality tracks whatever you wire it to, and the defaults are conservative in ways some people find slow — it asks before running tests and prefers small diffs. The interface is a prompt loop rather than an editor, which suits people who already live in a terminal and frustrates people who want to see a diff pane. MIT-licensed, actively maintained, self-hostable.
